edges.mechanism: American ginseng lowered peak INR (-0.19, 95% CI -0.36 to -0.07), INR AUC and plasma warfarin levels; Panax ginseng / Korean red ginseng showed no significant INR change in patients or healthy subjects.
edges.evidence: 1 RCT (American ginseng, n=20 healthy volunteers) positive; 3 RCTs with P. ginseng/KRG null; SR of herb-warfarin RCTs; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Case reports of interaction with phenelzine; systematic reviews report mania with concomitant phenelzine; pharmacodynamic CNS stimulation.
edges.evidence: Case reports summarized in systematic reviews; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Additive glucose lowering: FBG -0.31 mmol/L in MA; American ginseng reduced postprandial glycemia and lowered HbA1c 0.29% as add-on to conventional therapy; hypoglycemia listed as perioperative concern.
edges.evidence: MA of 16 RCTs, acute and 8-week crossover RCTs, review; low certainty

edges.mechanism: P. ginseng 500 mg twice daily for 28 days lowered midazolam AUC (GMR 0.66) consistent with weak CYP3A induction; red ginseng cocktail studies showed no clinically relevant CYP3A4 change.
edges.evidence: Open-label PK studies in healthy volunteers; product-dependent; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Probable interaction (Horn scale) causing acute hepatitis (ALT 1069 U/L) after 3 months of ginseng in energy drinks in a patient stable on imatinib for 7 years; proposed via CYP3A4; no recurrence on imatinib re-challenge without ginseng.
edges.evidence: Single case report; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Fermented red ginseng raised fexofenadine AUC (GMR 1.322); P. ginseng extract did not change fexofenadine pharmacokinetics.
edges.evidence: Two small PK studies with conflicting results; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Reviews list possible bleeding with ginseng, but an RCT found no added platelet inhibition with aspirin and no PT/APTT or thrombin-generation effect.
edges.evidence: RCT in healthy volunteers (n=25 per herb) plus reviews; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Immunostimulatory activity (TLR activation, NF-kB/MAPK, pro-inflammatory cytokines) could theoretically oppose immunosuppression.
edges.evidence: Mechanistic inference from scoping review; no clinical interaction study

edges.mechanism: Digoxin-like immunoreactive components of Asian/American ginseng falsely raise digoxin on FPIA and falsely lower it on MEIA; Tina-quant, LOCI and ARCHITECT assays largely free of interference.
edges.evidence: In vitro and mouse studies across multiple assays; moderate certainty for assay-dependence

edges.mechanism: Ginseng is co-formulated with caffeine in energy drinks; insomnia is ginseng's most common side effect, so additive stimulation/insomnia is plausible (mechanistic inference). The imatinib hepatotoxicity case involved ginseng taken via energy drinks.
edges.evidence: Mechanistic inference; position stand and case report; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Ashwagandha ('Indian ginseng') also produces digoxin-like immunoreactivity on FPIA/MEIA, and both are among the herbs with the strongest immunostimulatory evidence; additive assay interference and immunostimulation possible.
edges.evidence: In vitro assay studies and scoping review; mechanistic inference; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Overlapping adaptogen mechanisms (HPA-axis regulation, stress-response pathways); duplicate adaptogen stacking has no clinical interaction data.
edges.evidence: Mechanistic inference from reviews; no clinical interaction study

edges.mechanism: EU HMPC: not recommended for lack of adequate data; a ginsenoside caused birth defects in animals; systematic review advises caution especially in first trimester.
edges.evidence: Regulatory monograph, NCCIH fact sheet, systematic review; low certainty

edges.mechanism: No human lactation safety data; EU HMPC advises against use during breastfeeding.
edges.evidence: Regulatory monograph and systematic review; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: EU HMPC does not recommend use under 18 years because of lack of adequate data.
edges.evidence: Regulatory monograph

edges.mechanism: Ginseng implicated in 5 of 35 published herbal mania case reports; manic psychosis with high-dose chronic use remitting after withdrawal.
edges.evidence: Case reports and systematic review of case reports; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Older uncontrolled reports ('ginseng abuse syndrome') raised BP concern, but RCT meta-analyses show neutral or slightly lowering effects (SBP -2.57 mmHg); acute American ginseng neutral in hypertensive patients.
edges.evidence: MAs of RCTs and acute RCT; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Ginsenoside Rb1 is a weak ER-dependent phytoestrogen in vitro; case reports of mastalgia and postmenopausal vaginal bleeding; RCTs show no endometrial thickness change.
edges.evidence: In vitro study, case reports, SR of RCTs; conflicting; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Immunostimulatory activity; NCCIH notes ginseng may worsen autoimmune disorders.
edges.evidence: Scoping review and agency fact sheet; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Perioperative concerns: possible bleeding and hypoglycemia.
edges.evidence: Narrative review; very low certainty
